10	/-!
11	# The big-site Zariski sheaf `pic⁰` and the 01JJ seam (DAT-6, stage 3)
12	
13	The slice trick assembled: the Σ-extension of the degree-zero Picard functor is an
14	honest sheaf for the big Zariski topology on `Scheme`, and mathlib's 01JJ
15	local-representability engine applied to it descends to a representation of the
16	degree-zero Picard functor itself on the slice.
17	
18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0TypeFunctor C`: the degree-zero Picard functor with values in
19	  types — the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage of `pic0Functor`, owned here once
20	  (`pic0TypeFunctor_obj`/`pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply` are `rfl`).
21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0SigmaFunctor C : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u`: the Σ-extension
22	  `T ↦ Σ (a : T ⟶ Spec k), pic⁰(Over.mk a)` — the big-site carrier.
23	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf` / **`pic0SigmaSheaf C`**: the sheaf
24	  certificate.  By mathlib's own reduction the big-site sheaf condition collapses to
25	  elementwise ∃!-amalgamation on honest open covers
26	  (`Precoverage.isSheaf_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderBaseChange`,
27	  `exists_cover_of_mem_pretopology`, `Presieve.isSheafFor_arrows_iff` — the
28	  `BigZariski` TODO is never touched): the Σ-components glue by
29	  `Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms`, the fibre components glue by the DAT-6 stage-1
30	  evaluation bridge (`pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover`), and the two layers are
31	  stitched by the stage-2 amalgamation seam (`sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff`) and
32	  compatibility descent (`map_eq_of_sigmaExtension_map_eq`).
33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`: **the DAT-glue seam** — given a
34	  chart family of relatively representable open immersions into `pic0SigmaSheaf`
35	  (DAT-C) that is jointly locally surjective (DAT-B), mathlib's
36	  `Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy` produces a representation of the
37	  Σ-extension by the glued scheme, and the stage-2 Σ-descent `overSlice` turns it
38	  into a representation of `pic0TypeFunctor C` by the glued scheme over the
39	  Σ-component of the universal element.
40	-/

54	/-! ## The type-valued degree-zero Picard functor -/

56	/-- The degree-zero Picard functor with values in types: the `forget₂ ⋙ forget`
57	massage of `pic0Functor`, owned here once for the Σ-extension statements. -/
58	noncomputable abbrev pic0TypeFunctor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
59	  (pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat
60	
61	@[simp]
62	lemma pic0TypeFunctor_obj (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
63	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).obj T = pic0Subgroup C T.unop :=
64	  rfl
65	
66	lemma pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T')
67	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :
68	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).map g lam = pic0Map C g.unop lam :=
69	  rfl

71	/-! ## The Σ-extension as a presheaf on the big site -/
72	
73	/-- **The big-site carrier of the slice trick**: the Σ-extension of the type-valued
74	degree-zero Picard functor, `T ↦ Σ (a : T ⟶ Spec k), pic⁰(Over.mk a)`.  Reducible so
75	that the stage-2 `sigmaExtension` calculus applies syntactically. -/
76	noncomputable abbrev pic0SigmaFunctor : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
77	  Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (pic0TypeFunctor C)
78	
79	variable [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]
80	
81	set_option maxHeartbeats 800000 in
82	-- The amalgamation seams unify the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage of `pic0Functor`
83	-- against the Σ-extension calculus by unfolding; within the DAT-2/PicEtMap 1600000
84	-- precedent.
85	/-- **The big-site Zariski sheaf certificate of the Σ-extension** (DAT-6 keystone,
86	worksheet §1.2 site gap 1): mathlib's reduction collapses the sheaf condition to
87	elementwise ∃!-amalgamation on honest open covers, where the Σ-components glue by
88	`Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms` and the fibre components by the stage-1 evaluation
89	bridge. -/
90	theorem pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf :
91	    Presieve.IsSheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology (pic0SigmaFunctor C) := by
92	  rw [Precoverage.isSheaf_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderBaseChange]
93	  intro Y S hS
94	  obtain ⟨𝓤, rfl⟩ := Scheme.exists_cover_of_mem_pretopology hS
95	  rw [Presieve.isSheafFor_arrows_iff]
96	  intro x hx
97	  -- glue the Σ-components along the scheme-level cover
98	  have hpair : ∀ i j, pullback.fst (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j) ≫ (x i).1
99	      = pullback.snd (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j) ≫ (x j).1 := fun i j =>
100	    congrArg Sigma.fst
101	      (hx i j (pullback (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j)) (pullback.fst _ _) (pullback.snd _ _)
102	        pullback.condition)
103	  obtain ⟨aY, ha⟩ : ∃ aY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k), ∀ i, 𝓤.f i ≫ aY = (x i).1 :=
104	    ⟨𝓤.glueMorphisms (fun i => (x i).1) hpair,
105	      fun i => 𝓤.ι_glueMorphisms (fun i => (x i).1) hpair i⟩
106	  -- the induced slice cover of `Over.mk aY` and its member sections
107	  haveI hop : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion
108	      ((Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)).left :=
109	    fun i => 𝓤.map_prop i
110	  have hcov : ∀ p : (Over.mk aY).left, ∃ i, p ∈ Scheme.Hom.opensRange
111	      ((Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)).left := by
112	    intro p
113	    obtain ⟨i, y, hy⟩ := 𝓤.exists_eq p
114	    exact ⟨i, y, hy⟩
115	  -- the fibre components are a compatible family on the slice cover
116	  have hcompat : ∀ (i j : 𝓤.I₀) (Z : Over (Spec (.of k)))
117	      (gi : Z ⟶ Over.mk ((x i).1)) (gj : Z ⟶ Over.mk ((x j).1)),
118	      gi ≫ (Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)
119	          = gj ≫ (Over.homMk (𝓤.f j) (ha j) : Over.mk ((x j).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY) →
120	      pic0Map C gi ((x i).2) = pic0Map C gj ((x j).2) := by
121	    intro i j Z gi gj hg
122	    have hleft : gi.left ≫ 𝓤.f i = gj.left ≫ 𝓤.f j := congrArg Over.Hom.left hg
123	    have hdesc := Over.map_eq_of_sigmaExtension_map_eq gi gj
124	      (hx i j Z.left gi.left gj.left hleft)
125	    rwa [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply, pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply] at hdesc
126	  -- glue the fibre components by the stage-1 evaluation bridge
127	  obtain ⟨s, hs, hsu⟩ := pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover
128	    (fun i => (Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY))
129	    hcov (fun i => (x i).2) hcompat
130	  refine ⟨⟨aY, s⟩, fun i => ?_, ?_⟩
131	  · -- the glued Σ-element restricts to the members
132	    refine (Over.sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff (𝓤.f i) (ha i) s ((x i).2)).mpr ?_
133	    rw [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply]
134	    exact hs i
135	  · -- uniqueness: Σ-components by `hom_ext`, fibres by bridge separation
136	    rintro ⟨a', s'⟩ ht'
137	    obtain rfl : aY = a' := 𝓤.hom_ext aY a' fun i =>
138	      (ha i).trans (congrArg Sigma.fst (ht' i) : 𝓤.f i ≫ a' = (x i).1).symm
139	    refine congrArg (Sigma.mk aY) (hsu s' fun i => ?_)
140	    have hmem := (Over.sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff (𝓤.f i) (ha i) s' ((x i).2)).mp
141	      (ht' i)
142	    rwa [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply] at hmem
143	
144	/-- **The Σ-extension of the degree-zero Picard functor, bundled as a sheaf on the
145	big Zariski site** — the object mathlib's 01JJ local-representability engine
146	consumes. -/
147	noncomputable def pic0SigmaSheaf : Sheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology.{u} (Type u) :=
148	  ⟨pic0SigmaFunctor C,
149	    (isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_of_type _ _).mpr (pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf C)⟩
150	
151	/-! ## The DAT-glue seam -/
152	
153	/-- **The DAT-glue statement (worksheet §4, DAT-glue row)**: a chart family of
154	relatively representable open immersions into the Σ-extension sheaf (DAT-C's
155	certificates) that is jointly Zariski-locally surjective (DAT-B's coverage) induces —
156	through mathlib's 01JJ engine and the stage-2 Σ-descent — a representation of the
157	type-valued degree-zero Picard functor by the glued scheme placed over the
158	Σ-component of the universal element.  The represented object's `.left` is
159	`(Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued` and its `.hom` is the universal
160	element's Σ-component, both definitionally. -/
161	noncomputable def pic0RepresentableByOfCharts
162	    {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
163	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
164	    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i))
165	    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)] :
166	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy
167	      (Over.mk ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
168	        (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1) :=
169	  (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).overSlice
170

7	
8	/-!
9	# THE ATLAS IS CHART-PARAMETER HETEROGENEOUS — each chart may carry its own `n`
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack.lean` establishes that at a chart index legal at parameter
12	`n` the coverage theorem's threshold is forced to equal `n`, and that at `n = g` the resulting
13	hypothesis is false.  Both that file and the review it adjudicates (I-0660) then reason about
14	"the" chart parameter, as though the atlas had one.
15	
16	**It does not, and this file proves it.**  `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`
17	(`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) takes a family `f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ pic0SigmaSheaf`
18	indexed by an arbitrary `ι`, with `X : ι → Scheme` and a *per-index* certificate
19	`hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i)`.  Nothing ties the `X i` together, so nothing ties
20	their chart parameters together either: `mixedParamChart` below builds such a family from a
21	per-index parameter `nn : ι → ℕ`, a per-index representation of `divFunctor C π (nn i)`, and a
22	per-index chart index legal *at that index's own parameter*.
23	
24	## Why this matters, and it changes the shape of the residue
25	
26	The `b = n` calibration is per-chart.  So the question "can coverage use DAT-0a's threshold?"
27	does not have to be answered uniformly: a point whose splitting field has threshold `b_L` can be
28	covered by *the chart whose parameter is `b_L.toNat`*, and a different point by a different
29	chart.  The I-0204 non-uniformity of `m` — no single exponent works for every fibre — is
30	therefore **not** an obstruction to the atlas; it is an argument for an atlas indexed by the
31	threshold, which is what a heterogeneous family is.
32	
33	What this does **not** do, and the honest limit of the observation:
34	
35	* it does not produce the representations.  `mixedParamChart` takes `rep i` as a hypothesis, one
36	  per parameter, and the divisor-representability lane supplies `divFunctor C π g` — a single
37	  parameter.  So the heterogeneous atlas is *admissible* but not yet *inhabited* beyond `n = g`;
38	* it does not discharge `IsChartUniv` at any index (still CERT-Σ-gated, `Pic0ChartPair.lean`);
39	* it says nothing about local surjectivity, which is DAT-B B-6 and is what would actually consume
40	  the freedom.
41	
42	So the correct statement of the residue, refining `Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack`'s: **B-5's step 3
43	is a question about which parameters `divFunctor C π n` is representable at, not about
44	reconciling one parameter with one threshold.**  If representability is available only at `n = g`
45	then the slack must go into `Z` (and its legality is open, as recorded there); if it is available
46	at every `n`, coverage can be assembled chart-by-chart against each fibre's own threshold and the
47	`b = n` forcing is harmless.  That is a sharper question than either prior reading, and it is
48	addressed to the divRep lane rather than to this one.
49	
50	## Main declarations
51	
52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mixedParamChart` — a chart family with a per-index chart parameter.
53	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_mixedParamChart` — its `hf` clause is exactly a
54	  per-index `IsChartUniv`, so heterogeneity costs nothing in the certificate.
55	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mixedParamRepresentableBy` — such a family is admissible input to
56	  `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`.  **This is the whole point**: the DAT-glue seam never sees a
57	  chart parameter.
58	-/
59	
60	set_option autoImplicit false
61	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
62	
63	universe u
64	
65	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
66	
67	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
68	
69	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
70	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π]
71	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
72	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
73	
74	noncomputable section
75	
76	variable (C π) in
77	/-- **A chart family whose chart parameter varies with the index.**
78	
79	Each index `i` carries its own degree parameter `nn i`, its own representing object `D i` of
80	`divFunctor C π (nn i)`, its own twist exponent `m i` and chart index `Z i` — the latter legal
81	*at `nn i`*, i.e. `deg_k (Z i) = (m i)·d₁ − nn i`, which is what `chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup`
82	requires for that index's chart value to land in `pic⁰`.
83	
84	The construction is just `restrictChart` of `abelSigmaChart` applied pointwise; the content is
85	that it *typechecks*, i.e. that the target `pic0SigmaSheaf C` is parameter-free. -/
86	def mixedParamChart {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
87	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
88	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
89	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
90	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
91	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
92	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens) (i : ι) :
93	    yoneda.obj ((V i : Scheme.{u})) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 :=
94	  restrictChart (abelSigmaChart C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i)) (V i)
95	
96	variable (C π) in
97	/-- **Heterogeneity costs nothing in the certificate**: the `hf` clause of a mixed-parameter
98	family is exactly a per-index `IsChartUniv`, by definition of both.
99	
100	So a lane that can discharge CHART-U(c) *at one parameter* can discharge it index-by-index at
101	different parameters, with no additional compatibility between them — there is no coherence
102	condition across indices, because `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` imposes none. -/
103	theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_mixedParamChart {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
104	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
105	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
106	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
107	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
108	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
109	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens)
110	    (huniv : ∀ i, IsChartUniv C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i) (V i)) (i : ι) :
111	    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V i) :=
112	  huniv i
113	
114	variable (C π) in
115	/-- **A mixed-parameter chart family is admissible input to the DAT-glue seam.**
116	
117	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` accepts it verbatim.  This is the statement that settles the
118	question `Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack` and I-0660 both left implicit: the representability engine
119	never sees a chart parameter, so the forced calibration `b = n` is a *per-chart* condition and
120	carries no uniformity obligation.
121	
122	Note what remains hypothetical here and is not weakened by this: `hf` (i.e. `IsChartUniv`, still
123	CERT-Σ-gated), local surjectivity (DAT-B B-6), and the *existence* of `rep i` at parameters other
124	than `g` — which is the question this observation hands to the divisor-representability lane. -/
125	def mixedParamRepresentableBy {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
126	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
127	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
128	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
129	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
130	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
131	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens)
132	    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V i))
133	    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
134	      (Sigma.desc (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V))] :
135	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy
136	      (Over.mk ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
137	        (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1) :=
138	  pic0RepresentableByOfCharts C (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V) hf
139	
140	end

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivRepGlobalLift

/-!
# DDR-9.F7 — the affine-to-general lift, completed

`Picard/DivRepGlobalLift.lean` builds the general-test pullback `pullGlobal` of an
affine divisor package `DivRepAffinePullback` together with its naturality in the
test object.  This file supplies the other half — the general-test classifier — and
assembles the `DivRepGlobalData` of `Picard/DivRepKit.lean`, hence the divisor
representability of `divFunctor C π g` by `DivScheme`.

The classifier is obtained by gluing the landed affine classifiers `divRepClassifyZar`
over the affine opens of the test.  Two observations make the gluing cheap:

* The affine opens of a scheme form a **locally directed** open cover
  (`Scheme.directedAffineCover`), so a morphism glues from compatibility with the
  transition maps alone (`Scheme.OpenCover.glueMorphismsOverOfLocallyDirected`); no
  condition on the — in general non-affine — overlaps is needed.
* The required compatibility is naturality of `divRepClassifyZar` in the test algebra.
  That naturality is not proved from the characterizing clause: it is *forced* by the
  affine package, since `D.pull` is injective (`DivRepAffinePullback.equiv`) and natural
  (`D.pull_naturality`), so the classifier — its inverse — is natural as well.

The results:

* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivRepAffinePullback.classifyGlobal` — the general-test classifier,
  restricting at every affine open `W ⊆ T.left` to the affine classifier of the value
  `F.1 W` (`fromSpecAffine_classifyGlobal`).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivRepAffinePullback.toGlobalData` — the `DivRepGlobalData` of the
  affine package: `pullGlobal` and `classifyGlobal` are mutually inverse on every test.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivRepAffinePullback.representableBy` — **the divisor
  representability theorem in its conditional form**: an affine divisor package
  represents `divFunctor C π g` by `DivScheme`.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option quotPrecheck false
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

universe u

open CategoryTheory

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

open Grassmannian Scheme

attribute [local instance] Over.sectionsAlgebra

/-! ## Separation over the affine opens of a test object -/

section Separation

variable {k : Type u} [Field k]

/-- The comparison isomorphism of an affine open with the spectrum of its section ring
carries `IsAffineOpen.fromSpec` to the open immersion of the open. -/
private theorem isoSpec_hom_fromSpec {X : Scheme.{u}} {U : X.Opens} (hU : IsAffineOpen U) :
    hU.isoSpec.hom ≫ hU.fromSpec = U.ι := by
  rw [← IsAffineOpen.isoSpec_inv_ι, Iso.hom_inv_id_assoc]

/-- **Separation of test objects over their affine-open test objects**: two morphisms
out of a test object `T` agreeing on every affine-open test object `Over.fromSpecAffine T U`
are equal.  The affine opens cover `T.left`, and `fromSpecAffine T U` differs from the
open immersion of `U` by the comparison isomorphism of `U`. -/
private theorem hom_ext_fromSpecAffine {T Y : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (a b : T ⟶ Y)
    (h : ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens,
      Over.fromSpecAffine T U ≫ a = Over.fromSpecAffine T U ≫ b) :
    a = b := by
  refine Over.OverMorphism.ext ?_
  refine Scheme.Cover.hom_ext T.left.directedAffineCover _ _ fun U => ?_
  have hU : U.2.fromSpec ≫ a.left = U.2.fromSpec ≫ b.left :=
    congrArg CategoryTheory.Over.Hom.left (h U)
  change U.1.ι ≫ a.left = U.1.ι ≫ b.left

/-- Compatibility may be applied when both chart presentations are identified with a
common morphism.  This is the form used on overlaps of an atlas factorization. -/
theorem pullAt_eq_of_eq_common
    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
      DivFamZar C (ChartRing i j) pi g)
    (hU : IsCompatible (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U)
    {S : Type u} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
    (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J)
    (i' : (glueData k g r1).J) (j' : (glueData k g r2).J)
    (omega : ChartRing i j →ₐ[k] S) (omega' : ChartRing i' j' →ₐ[k] S)
    (q : Spec (CommRingCat.of S) ⟶
      DivScheme k (windowS_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi)
        (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) g r1 r2 b1
        (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm))
    (homega : Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom omega.toRingHom) ≫ ChartMap i j = q)
    (homega' : Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom omega'.toRingHom) ≫ ChartMap i' j' = q) :
    divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i j omega
      = divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i' j' omega' :=
  hU i j i' j' omega omega' (homega.trans homega'.symm)

end DivRepChartFamily

/-! ## F6: package a completed affine pullback as an equivalence -/

/-- The exact output expected from F5 before the affine equivalence is packaged.
`isDivRepClassify_pull` is the hom-side law in the refinement-stable clause spelling;
classifier uniqueness turns it into the second inverse law automatically. -/
structure DivRepAffinePullback where
  pull : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S],
    (overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver) → DivFamZar C S pi g
  pull_classify : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
    (F : DivFamZar C S pi g),
    pull S (divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 S F) = F
  isDivRepClassify_pull : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
    (v : overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver),
    IsDivRepClassify hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 (pull S v) v.left
  pull_naturality : ∀ {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (phi : A →ₐ[k] B) (v : overSpec k A ⟶ DivOver),
    pull B (Over.overSpecMap phi ≫ v) = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom phi (pull A v)

namespace DivRepAffinePullback

/-- The affine representability equivalence assembled from an F5 pullback package.
The inverse is the landed backward classifier; its hom-side inverse law follows from
`divRepClassifyZar_eq_of_isDivRepClassify`. -/
noncomputable def equiv
    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] :
    (overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver) ≃ DivFamZar C S pi g where
  toFun := D.pull S
  invFun := divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 S
  left_inv v :=
    (divRepClassifyZar_eq_of_isDivRepClassify hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2
      (D.pull S v) v (D.isDivRepClassify_pull S v)).symm
  right_inv := D.pull_classify S

@[simp]
theorem equiv_apply
    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] (v : overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver) :
    equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
        (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D S v = D.pull S v :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem equiv_symm_apply
    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] (F : DivFamZar C S pi g) :
    (equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
      (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D S).symm F
      = divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 S F :=
  rfl

/-- Naturality of the assembled affine equivalence, in the frozen DDR-9 spelling. -/
theorem equiv_naturality
    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (phi : A →ₐ[k] B)
    (v : overSpec k A ⟶ DivOver) :
    equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
        (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D B (Over.overSpecMap phi ≫ v)
      = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom phi
          (equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
            (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D A v) :=
  D.pull_naturality phi v

end DivRepAffinePullback

end Curve

end AlgebraicGeometry

over `T` and the chart data over `Localization.Away (f t)` classify the same restricted
class, and `pullback_chart_divClassifyClause_compat` identifies their morphisms on the
overlap; `Scheme.Cover.hom_ext` over the pulled-back factorization cover globalizes. -/
theorem isDivRepClassify_divRepPullValue
    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
      DivFamZar C (ChartRing i j) pi g)
    (hU : DivRepChartFamily.IsChartClause (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U)
    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] (v : overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver) :
    IsDivRepClassify hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2
      (divRepPullValue hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 U
        (DivRepChartFamily.IsChartClause.isCompatible hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 hU)
        S v) v.left := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨m, f, hspan, ci, cj, cw, hcw, hF⟩ :=
    divRepPullValue_spec hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 U
      (DivRepChartFamily.IsChartClause.isCompatible hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 hU) S v
  refine isDivRepClassify_of_forall_away hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 _ _ f hspan fun t => ?_
  -- on the `t`-th piece the value IS the chart pull, and the chart morphism IS the
  -- restriction of `v.left` — so the chart clause is literally the piecewise statement.
  -- The face-change bridge moves `hF`'s explicit `mapAlgHom` onto the instance face.
  rw [← DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_eq_mapAlg
      (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k S (Localization.Away (f t))) (fun _ => rfl), hF t,
    ← hcw t]
  exact hU (ci t) (cj t) (cw t)

/-! ## The producer: `IsChartClause` is the whole remaining debt -/

include hO hchi in
/-- **A `DivRepAffinePullback` from `IsChartClause` alone** — the point of this file.

`DivRepAffinePullback.ofPull` asks for three fields; all three are now available from the
single per-chart ε clause:

* `pull` is `divRepPullValue`, whose conditionality on `IsCompatible` is discharged by
  `IsChartClause.isCompatible`;
* `isDivRepClassify_pull` is `isDivRepClassify_divRepPullValue`;
* `pull_naturality` is `divRepPullValue_naturality` (ε-free);

and `pull_classify` is derived by the separation theorem.  Composing with
`DivRepAffinePullback.representableBy` (`Picard/DivRepGlobalClassify.lean`) this turns the
DDR9-U ε-identity into the *only* remaining input of divisor representability. -/
noncomputable def divRepAffinePullback_ofChartClause
    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
      DivFamZar C (ChartRing i j) pi g)
    (hU : DivRepChartFamily.IsChartClause (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U) :
    DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 :=
  DivRepAffinePullback.ofPull hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2
    (fun S _ _ => divRepPullValue hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 U
      (DivRepChartFamily.IsChartClause.isCompatible hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 hU) S)
    (fun S _ _ v =>
      isDivRepClassify_divRepPullValue hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 U hU S v)
======== Reduce ========
      DivFamZar C (ChartRing i j) pi g)
    (hcl : ∀ {S : Type u} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
      (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J)
      (omega : ChartRing i j →ₐ[k] S),
      IsDivRepClassify hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2
        (divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i j omega)
        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom omega.toRingHom) ≫ ChartMap i j)) :
    DivRepChartFamily.IsCompatible (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U := by
  intro S _ _ i j i' j' omega omega' hq
  refine eq_of_isDivRepClassify hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 _ _ (v := ?_) ?_ ?_
  · exact Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom omega.toRingHom) ≫ ChartMap i j
  · exact hcl i j omega
  · exact hq ▸ hcl i' j' omega'

include hO hchi in
/-- **The round-trip law is free once the clause law holds** (F6, via the separation
theorem): if `pull` produces, for every morphism `v`, a class classified by `v`, then it
inverts the backward classifier.

Both `pull S (divRepClassifyZar F)` and `F` satisfy the characterizing clause for the
single morphism `divRepClassifyZar F` — the first by hypothesis, the second by
`divRepClassifyZar_isDivRepClassify` — so `eq_of_isDivRepClassify` identifies them. -/
theorem pull_classify_of_isDivRepClassify_pull
    (pull : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S],
      (overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver) → DivFamZar C S pi g)
    (hpull : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] (v : overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver),
      IsDivRepClassify hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 (pull S v) v.left)
    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] (F : DivFamZar C S pi g) :
    pull S (divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 S F) = F :=
  eq_of_isDivRepClassify hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 _ F
    (hpull S (divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 S F))
    (divRepClassifyZar_isDivRepClassify hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 F)

namespace DivRepAffinePullback

include hO hchi in
/-- **The three-field constructor of `DivRepAffinePullback`**: the `pull_classify` field is
derived from `isDivRepClassify_pull` by `pull_classify_of_isDivRepClassify_pull`, so a
producer owes only the pullback map, the characterizing clause it satisfies, and
naturality. -/
noncomputable def ofPull
    (pull : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S],
      (overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver) → DivFamZar C S pi g)
    (hpull : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] (v : overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver),
      IsDivRepClassify hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 (pull S v) v.left)
    (hnat : ∀ {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
      (phi : A →ₐ[k] B) (v : overSpec k A ⟶ DivOver),
      pull B (Over.overSpecMap phi ≫ v) = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom phi (pull A v)) :
    DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 where
  pull := pull
  pull_classify := pull_classify_of_isDivRepClassify_pull hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2
    pull hpull
  isDivRepClassify_pull := hpull
  pull_naturality := hnat

set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
@[simp]
theorem ofPull_pull
    (pull : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S],
      (overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver) → DivFamZar C S pi g)
    (hpull : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] (v : overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver),
      IsDivRepClassify hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 (pull S v) v.left)
    (hnat : ∀ {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
      (phi : A →ₐ[k] B) (v : overSpec k A ⟶ DivOver),
      pull B (Over.overSpecMap phi ≫ v) = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom phi (pull A v))
    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] (v : overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver) :
    (ofPull hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 pull hpull hnat).pull S v = pull S v :=
  rfl

end DivRepAffinePullback

AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:205:def abelSigmaChart {D : Over (Spec (.of k))} (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0ChartPair.lean:120:def restrictChart {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0ChartPair.lean:173:def IsChartUniv {D : Over (Spec (.of k))} (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)

1	/-

4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
5	-/
6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0AtlasFromDivRep
8	
9	/-!
10	# C9b: the restricted chart map and the `(f, hf)` pair
11	
12	`Picard/Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean` builds the Abel chart map `abelSigmaChart` out of a
13	representation of the divisor functor, and its header states — correctly — that
14	`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (abelSigmaChart …)` is **false as stated for the whole divisor
15	scheme**: the Abel map has projective spaces `|D|` as fibres, so it is not even a
16	monomorphism.  It becomes an open immersion only after restriction to the locus where the
17	fibre is a single point.
18	
19	This file supplies the restriction, which is the half of C9b that needs no new mathematics
20	once `chartLocus` exists — and it makes precise which half does.
21	
22	## What C9b consists of, and which part is here
23	
24	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` (`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) consumes a pair
25	`(f, hf)`.  Producing it from `abelSigmaChart` factors into exactly two steps:
26	
27	1. **restrict the source along an open immersion** — `restrictChart` below.  Given any open
28	   `V ⊆ D.left`, precomposing `abelSigmaChart` with `yoneda.map V.ι` gives a chart map out of
29	   `V`, and this is a *composition* of presheaf morphisms.  Landed here, sorry-free.
30	2. **certify the restricted map an open immersion of presheaves** — the honest content.
31	   `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` (mathlib `MorphismProperty.relative`) has two clauses:
32	   relative representability, and the open-immersion property of every represented pullback.
33	   Step 1 supplies the *left* factor of both clauses for free
34	   (`isOpenImmersion_presheaf_yoneda_map_of_isOpenImmersion` +
35	   `MorphismProperty.relative_isStableUnderComposition`), so what remains is exactly the
36	   corresponding statement for `abelSigmaChart` restricted to `V = chartLocus`, i.e.
37	   CHART-U(c): on the chart locus the Abel map is a bijection onto its image because the
38	   normalized effective representative is unique there (DAT-C GAP-2).
39	
40	So: the *composition* half of the `hf` certificate is discharged here, unconditionally; the
41	*chart-locus* half is CHART-U(c) and is stated but not proved (it needs GAP-2 plus the
42	classifier, and the openness of the locus itself, `Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`).
43	
44	## CORRECTION 2026-07-29: step 2 above is itself TWO clauses, not one
45	
46	The description of step 2 as "*the* honest content" is right that it is not bookkeeping and
47	wrong that it is a single obligation.  `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` conjoins **relative
48	representability** (the fibre product is a scheme at all) with **the property clause** (each
49	represented pullback is an open immersion).  The GAP-2/classifier story is the input to the
50	second only.  The first needs just an open of the test, and `chartLocus` is one
51	unconditionally — so it is not CERT-Σ-gated at all.
52	
53	That split is landed: `Picard/Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean` (the criterion, from
54	elementwise data) and `Picard/Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean` (instantiated at the Abel chart,
55	reducing the datum from four fields to three).  `IsChartUniv` below is unchanged as a
56	*statement* — it is still the right pin — but it is no longer the right unit of *pricing*.
57	Read `isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre` for what a lane now actually owes.
58	
59	## Main declarations
60	
61	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_yoneda_map` — an open immersion of schemes is
62	  an open immersion of presheaves under yoneda.  This is mathlib's `relative_map` at
63	  `P := IsOpenImmersion`, recorded once with the instances it needs discharged.
64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.restrictChart` — the chart map restricted to an open of the source.
65	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart` — **the composition half of
66	  `hf`**: if the unrestricted chart map is an open immersion of presheaves, so is any
67	  restriction of it along an open immersion.  Unconditional in the restriction.
68	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartHom_restrictChart` — the structure morphism of a restricted chart
69	  is the restriction of the structure morphism, so the `LocallyOfFiniteType` hypothesis of
70	  `JacobianData.ofCharts` is inherited (being locally of finite type is local on the
71	  source).
72	-/
73	
74	set_option autoImplicit false
75	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
76	
77	universe u
78	
79	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
80	
81	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
82	
83	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
84	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π] {n : ℕ}
85	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
86	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
87	
88	noncomputable section
89	
90	/-! ## An open immersion of schemes is one of presheaves -/
91	
92	/-- **Open immersions transfer through yoneda**: for an open immersion of schemes
93	`g : X ⟶ Y`, the induced map of yoneda presheaves satisfies `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf`.
94	
95	This is mathlib's `MorphismProperty.relative_map` specialised to `F := yoneda` and
96	`P := @IsOpenImmersion`; the two side conditions it needs — that open immersions are stable
97	under base change, and that yoneda preserves the relevant pullbacks (it is fully faithful and
98	`Scheme` has pullbacks) — are discharged by instances.
99	
100	Recorded as a named lemma because it is the *only* source of `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf`
101	facts anywhere in this tree that does not go through a chart certificate: every restriction
102	of a chart map is built from it. -/
103	theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_yoneda_map {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (g : X ⟶ Y)
104	    [IsOpenImmersion g] :
105	    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (yoneda.map g) :=
106	  MorphismProperty.relative_map (P := @IsOpenImmersion) (F := yoneda) ‹IsOpenImmersion g›
107	
108	/-! ## The restricted chart map -/
109	
110	/-- **The chart map restricted to an open of its source.**
111	
112	`f` is the unrestricted chart map (in practice `abelSigmaChart`, whose source is the divisor
113	scheme) and `V` an open subscheme of the source; the restriction is the composition with the
114	yoneda image of the open inclusion.
115	
116	The point of restricting is that the unrestricted Abel map is *not* an open immersion of
117	presheaves — see the `Pic0AtlasFromDivRep` header — while its restriction to the locus where
118	the fibre is a single point is.  This definition is neutral about which open `V` is; the
119	chart-locus choice enters only in the certificate. -/
120	def restrictChart {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
121	    (V : X.Opens) : yoneda.obj (V : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 :=
122	  yoneda.map V.ι ≫ f
123	
124	/-- **The composition half of the `hf` certificate**: a restriction of an open immersion of
125	presheaves along an open immersion is again one.
126	
127	`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is `MorphismProperty.relative` at `yoneda`, which is stable under
128	composition (`MorphismProperty.relative_isStableUnderComposition`, needing `yoneda` full and
129	faithful and `IsOpenImmersion` stable under composition — all instances).  Together with
130	`isOpenImmersion_presheaf_yoneda_map` this discharges, for free and in full generality, the
131	part of C9b that is bookkeeping.
132	
133	What it does NOT discharge, and what is therefore the whole remaining content of C9b: the
134	hypothesis `hfV`.  For `f := abelSigmaChart` that hypothesis is FALSE for `V = ⊤` and is
135	expected to be true for `V = chartLocus` — it is CHART-U(c), whose proof needs the
136	uniqueness of the normalized effective representative (DAT-C GAP-2) and the classifier.  A
137	lane must not read this lemma as reducing C9b to plumbing; it isolates the plumbing so the
138	mathematics is visible. -/
139	theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart {X : Scheme.{u}}
140	    {f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1} (V : X.Opens)
141	    (hfV : IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f) :
142	    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (restrictChart f V) :=
143	  MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderComposition.comp_mem _ _
144	    (isOpenImmersion_presheaf_yoneda_map V.ι) hfV
145	
146	/-! ## CHART-U(c): the remaining obligation, pinned
147	
148	With the composition half discharged, `hf` for a restricted Abel chart reduces to a single
149	statement.  It is pinned here as a definition so that the gate has a name in Lean and not
150	only in a worksheet — the pattern `Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen.IsChartDatumPresentation` uses.
151	
152	**Its field-level input is available.**  DAT-C GAP-2 (Σ-UNIQ-fld) is *landed*:
153	`Scheme.CurveDivisor.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_h0_one`
154	(`RiemannRoch/EffectiveUniqueness.lean:144`) — for effective `D`, `D'` with equal Čech class
155	and `h⁰(𝒪(D)) = 1`, `D' = D`.  (The `w4-datc` §0.3 GAP-2 row claimed no such lemma existed;
156	that claim was stale and is corrected there as of 2026-07-28.)  What CHART-U(c) still needs
157	beyond it is the *relative* statement — uniqueness in families over the locus — plus the
158	classifier `divRepClassifyZar`. -/
159	
160	variable (C π n) in
161	/-- **CHART-U(c), pinned**: the chart map is an open immersion of presheaves after restriction
162	to the locus where the fibre class has a unique effective representative.
163	
164	This is the whole remaining content of C9b's `hf`.  Stated as a `Prop`-valued definition
165	rather than proved, because its proof needs the *relative* form of GAP-2 over `chartLocus`
166	together with `divRepClassifyZar`; a lane that discharges it gets `hf` by feeding it to
167	`isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart`.
168	
169	Deliberately stated about `abelSigmaChart` and a *given* open `V`, rather than about
170	`chartLocus` directly: the openness of `chartLocus` is a separate obligation
171	(`Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`), and keeping the two apart means neither has to wait for the
172	other. -/
173	def IsChartUniv {D : Over (Spec (.of k))} (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
174	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
175	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
176	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
177	    (V : D.left.Opens) : Prop :=
178	  IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (restrictChart (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg) V)
179	
180	/-- The pinned obligation is exactly what `isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart` would
181	give from an unrestricted certificate — recorded so that no lane proves the same thing
182	twice, and so that the *reason* the unrestricted route is unavailable stays visible: the
183	hypothesis of that lemma is false for the Abel chart at `V = ⊤`. -/
184	lemma isChartUniv_of_unrestricted {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
185	    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
186	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
187	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
188	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
189	    (V : D.left.Opens)
190	    (h : IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg)) :
191	    IsChartUniv C π n rep m Z hdeg V :=
192	  isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart V h
193	
194	/-! ## The structure morphism of a restricted chart -/
195	
196	/-- **The structure morphism of a restricted chart is the restriction of the structure
197	morphism.**  Hence the `LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom …)` hypothesis of
198	`JacobianData.ofCharts` is inherited by every restriction: being locally of finite type is
199	local on the source, and an open immersion is locally of finite type.
200	
201	Concretely, for the Abel chart of a representation `rep` by `D` the unrestricted structure
202	morphism is `D.hom` (`chartHom_abelSigmaChart`, `Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:212`), so a
203	restricted Abel chart over `V ⊆ D.left` has structure morphism `V.ι ≫ D.hom`. -/
204	lemma chartHom_restrictChart {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
205	    (V : X.Opens) {ι : Type u} (i : ι) :
206	    chartHom C (fun _ : ι => restrictChart f V) i
207	      = V.ι ≫ chartHom C (fun _ : ι => f) i := by
208	  change (yonedaEquiv (yoneda.map V.ι ≫ f)).1 = V.ι ≫ (yonedaEquiv f).1
209	  -- Both sides are the Σ-component of the universal element restricted along `V.ι`:
210	  -- the `Over.sigmaExtension` transition map precomposes the structure morphism, and
211	  -- `f`'s naturality moves the restriction across `f`.
212	  rw [yonedaEquiv_comp, yonedaEquiv_yoneda_map]
213	  have hnat := congrArg Sigma.fst
214	    (ConcreteCategory.congr_hom (f.naturality (V.ι).op) (𝟙 X))
215	  refine hnat.trans ?_
216	  exact Over.sigmaExtension_map_fst (V.ι) _
217	
218	end
219	
220	end AlgebraicGeometry

* chartsCoverLocally_of_affineLocal + mem_zariskiTopology_of_pullback_affine (Pic0ChartCoverageAffineTest.lean, 8ef1105ff) — antecedent 2's pointwise datum needs AFFINE tests only. FAMILY-GENERIC (arbitrary f), so it applies verbatim to mixedParamChart at any V. Rationale in I-1036.
* slice_iff_bare + datum_of_slice/bare_of_slice (Pic0ChartCoverageSlice.lean, 22d4cf035, e7f140babb).

REFUTED, MY OWN: 'the Sigma-component is absorbed by a slice morphism, leaving one class equation'. Over.mk (W.iota >> s.1) --> D IS the pair (x,hx) — both (Over.homMk x hx).left = x and Over.w (Over.homMk x hx) = hx are rfl — so the hypotheses are interderivable. Caught by work-reviewer (I-1021); lesson I-1024. My own non-vacuity check (rfl FAILS there) is what refutes the discount and I read it as licensing one.

ALSO CORRECTED: that file's converse is rfl-equal to pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally with [IsAffine] unused, certifying the FREE direction (I-1023). The affine form is a genuine weakening — which is why the forward theorem is the content.

THE RESIDUE, stated where the producers live: for an AFFINE test Y and point y, produce a divisor family over an open W containing y whose chart value is the given class restricted. Cost is a spreading-out — family over a NEIGHBOURHOOD from POINT data — measured ABSENT for this carrier by two independent censuses. Every DivFamZar producer takes its base ring or the affine-opens limit first; the only spreading lemmas (exists_supportTube, its Confine instance) act on the support locus of a given local-equation system; mathlib's spread_out_of_isGermInjective' is about morphism germs.

HARDER LIMIT, from p1's I-1017/I-1012: nothing pins V, hf is free at bot, top is refuted, so any workable V is a proper intermediate open and (huniv V, hcov V) has NO measured inhabitant at ANY V. Settle that before building coverage machinery.
--- comment: CARRIED FORWARD from I-0963 before archiving it as consumed (janitor, run 0088).

I-0963 held one measurement present in no other open item and absent from the dat-b row: the census
that locates this release's residue. Every candidate producer in Picard/ stops at `t \in chartLocus`,
a `Set T.left` membership, and none produces the morphism $x : (W : Scheme) \to X_i$ the coverage
datum needs. Strongest candidate `mem_chartLocus_of_witness_h1` (Pic0ChartCoverageNoDrop.lean:106),
sorry-free and general-test, concludes a Prop about one point. A chart-value equation in a CONCLUSION
has zero hits outside the reduction files, where it is a bound hypothesis. This is the evidence for
the 'measured ABSENT for this carrier' claim above.

The rest of I-0963 is preserved: the reduction chain in the dat-b row, the `ledger_forces_b_eq_n`
threshold refutation in open I-0929/I-0935/I-0948, the \iota = PEmpty degeneracy in open
I-0861/I-1023/I-1036.

I am measuring the two monotonicities and, if they hold, landing the two-open assembly.

I go first on it because it is a defect in MY file and MY row, and because the answer changes what p2's coverage lane owes: coverage may pick its own (smaller) open.

8	/-!
9	# C9b: what `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` of a chart map actually asks for
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartPair.lean` pins `IsChartUniv` — the `hf` half of the `(f, hf)` pair that
12	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes — and its docstring, together with the `c9b` roadmap
13	row, prices it as **one** obligation: the relative form of DAT-C GAP-2 plus the classifier,
14	CERT-Σ-gated.
15	
16	**That pricing is wrong, and this file is the correction.**  `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is
17	`MorphismProperty.relative` at `yoneda` (mathlib `MorphismProperty/Representable.lean`), and
18	`relative` is *by definition* a conjunction of two independent statements:
19	
20	1. **relative representability** — for every test `T` and every `g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ 𝓟`, the
21	   fibre product of the chart map along `g` is representable *by a scheme*;
22	2. **the property clause** — every represented pullback is an open immersion of schemes.
23	
24	The GAP-2/classifier story is the input to (2) only: it is what makes the fibre a single
25	point, hence the represented pullback an open subscheme.  It says nothing about (1), which
26	is a representability statement about a fibre product.  Read as one clause, a lane waits on
27	CERT-Σ for both halves.  Read as two, half of the work is stateable and provable *now*, with
28	no divisor-representability endpoint and no certificate anywhere in it.
29	
30	## What this file provides, and what it deliberately does not
31	
32	Everything here is stated for an **arbitrary** morphism of big-site presheaves
33	`f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1` and an **arbitrary** open `V ⊆ X`.  No `divRep`
34	endpoint, no certificate, no `Z`, no `θ` and no chart index appears in any statement.  That
35	is the point: `IsChartUniv` becomes *this criterion instantiated at* `abelSigmaChart`, and
36	the divisor-representability shape enters only at the instantiation.
37	
38	The criterion's hypotheses are **elementwise** conditions on the presheaf — a fibrewise
39	injectivity clause and a clause producing the representing open — because that is what
40	mathlib's `MorphismProperty.relative.of_exists` reduces the goal to once the presheaf
41	category's pullbacks are computed pointwise (`Types.isPullback_iff`).
42	
43	## Main declarations
44	
45	* `AlgebraicGeometry.ChartFibrePresented` — the elementwise datum (1) needs: for each test
46	  point `g` of the target, an open `W` of the test and an identification of the `W`-points
47	  with the chart points hitting `g`.  This is the *shape* of a fibre-product presentation,
48	  named so that a producer knows exactly what it owes.
49	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented` — **the criterion**:
50	  a `ChartFibrePresented` datum gives `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f`, discharging BOTH clauses
51	  at once.  Certificate-free and divRep-free.
52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mono_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf` — the converse direction that makes
53	  the split honest: `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f` *implies* `f` is a monomorphism.  So "the
54	  Abel map is not a monomorphism", which three files cite as the reason the unrestricted
55	  certificate fails, is a consequence of the criterion rather than an extra obligation — and
56	  it shows the elementwise injectivity clause below is **necessary**, not an artefact of
57	  this route.
58	* `AlgebraicGeometry.injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf` — the same fact in the
59	  elementwise form a chart-locus argument can actually use.
60	-/

63	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

71	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}

77	/-! ## The necessary direction: an open immersion of presheaves is a monomorphism
78	
79	Stated first, because it is what tells us the criterion below asks for the right thing. -/
80	
81	/-- **An open immersion of presheaves out of a representable is a monomorphism.**
82	
83	This is mathlib's `presheaf_mono_of_le` at `P := IsOpenImmersion`, whose hypothesis
84	`IsOpenImmersion ≤ monomorphisms Scheme` is the landed `IsOpenImmersion.le_monomorphisms`.
85	
86	Recorded because the whole chart layer rests on the sentence "the Abel map is not a
87	monomorphism, so `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is false for the unrestricted divisor scheme"
88	(`Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:54`, repeated in `Pic0ChartPair.lean:14`).  That sentence is a
89	*derivation*, not an independent input, and this lemma is the derivation. -/
90	theorem mono_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf {X : Scheme.{u}}
91	    {f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1} (hf : IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f) :
92	    Mono f :=
93	  MorphismProperty.presheaf_mono_of_le IsOpenImmersion.le_monomorphisms hf
94	
95	/-- **The elementwise form of the necessary direction**: if `f` is an open immersion of
96	presheaves then on every test it is injective on points.
97	
98	This is the clause `ChartFibrePresented.fibre_injective` below, read backwards, and it is
99	why that clause is not an artefact of this particular route: any proof of
100	`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f` whatsoever yields it.  For the Abel chart it is exactly "the
101	normalized effective representative is unique", i.e. the relative form of DAT-C GAP-2 — so
102	GAP-2 is *forced* by the target, not merely sufficient for it. -/
103	theorem injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf {X : Scheme.{u}}
104	    {f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1} (hf : IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f)
105	    (T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ) :
106	    Function.Injective (f.app T) :=
107	  (mono_iff_injective (f.app T)).mp
108	    ((NatTrans.mono_iff_mono_app f).mp (mono_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf hf) T)
109	
110	/-! ## The sufficient direction: the elementwise datum, and the criterion -/
111	
112	variable (C) in
113	/-- **The fibre of a chart map over one test point, presented by an open of the test.**
114	
115	This is the datum mathlib's `relative.of_exists` asks for at a single
116	`g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ pic0SigmaSheaf C`, written out so a producer can see exactly what it
117	owes.  Given a chart map `f` out of `X`:
118	
119	* `W` is an open subscheme of the test `T` — the locus where the class named by `g` *is* a
120	  chart value.  For the Abel chart this is `chartLocus`;
121	* `r` recovers the chart point: over `W`, the divisor family whose class `g` is;
122	* `sq` says the two ways round agree;
123	* `exists_factor` is the honest content — a test point of `X` and a test point of `T` with
124	  the *same* class come from a unique point of `W`.  Existence is coverage-on-the-locus;
125	  the uniqueness half is *not* a field here, because it is free: `W.ι` is a monomorphism.
126	
127	Nothing in this structure mentions a divisor scheme, a certificate, a twist or a chart
128	index.  It is a statement about a morphism of presheaves and an open of a test. -/
129	structure ChartFibrePresented {X T : Scheme.{u}}
130	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
131	    where
132	  /-- The locus of the test where the class named by `g` is a chart value. -/
133	  W : T.Opens
134	  /-- The chart point over that locus. -/
135	  r : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X
136	  /-- The square commutes: `r` names the class `g` restricted to `W`. -/
137	  sq : yoneda.map r ≫ f = yoneda.map W.ι ≫ g
138	  /-- **Coverage on the locus**: an `S`-point of `X` and an `S`-point of `T` carrying the
139	  same class factor through `W`, compatibly with both projections. -/
140	  exists_factor : ∀ (S : Scheme.{u}) (v : S ⟶ X) (w : S ⟶ T),
141	    f.app (op S) v = g.app (op S) w → ∃ u : S ⟶ (W : Scheme.{u}), u ≫ r = v ∧ u ≫ W.ι = w
142	
143	namespace ChartFibrePresented
144	
145	variable {X T : Scheme.{u}} {f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1}
146	  {g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1}
147	
148	/-- **The datum presents the fibre product**: the square of `ChartFibrePresented` is a
149	pullback of presheaves.
150	
151	Pullbacks in a presheaf category are computed pointwise
152	(`IsPullback.of_forall_isPullback_app`), and a pointwise pullback of types is exactly
153	"commutes + jointly injective + jointly surjective" (`Types.isPullback_iff`).  The first is
154	`sq`, the third is `exists_factor`, and the second is free from `W.ι` being a
155	monomorphism — which is where the openness of `W` does its work. -/
156	theorem isPullback (D : ChartFibrePresented C f g) :
157	    IsPullback (yoneda.map D.r) (yoneda.map D.W.ι) f g := by
158	  refine IsPullback.of_forall_isPullback_app fun S => ?_
159	  rw [Types.isPullback_iff]
160	  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
161	  · exact congrArg (fun φ : yoneda.obj (D.W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 =>
162	      φ.app S) D.sq
163	  · -- joint injectivity: already forced by `W.ι` alone, being a monomorphism
164	    rintro u₁ u₂ ⟨-, h₂⟩
165	    have : u₁ ≫ D.W.ι = u₂ ≫ D.W.ι := h₂
166	    exact (cancel_mono D.W.ι).mp this
167	  · -- joint surjectivity: `exists_factor` at the test `S.unop`
168	    intro v w hvw
169	    obtain ⟨u, hu₁, hu₂⟩ := D.exists_factor S.unop v w hvw
170	    exact ⟨u, hu₁, hu₂⟩
171	
172	end ChartFibrePresented
173	
174	/-- **THE CRITERION** — `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` from elementwise data, discharging BOTH
175	clauses of `MorphismProperty.relative` at once.
176	
177	Given, for every test point of the target sheaf, a `ChartFibrePresented` datum, the chart map
178	is an open immersion of presheaves.  Certificate-free, divRep-free, and with no reference to
179	divisors: the input is a family of opens of tests together with the coverage statement on
180	each.
181	
182	This is the honest shape of `IsChartUniv`'s obligation.  Reading `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf`
183	as a single "relative GAP-2" statement conflates:
184	
185	* **relative representability** — that the fibre product is a scheme at all.  Supplied here
186	  by `W`, an open subscheme of the test, and proved by `ChartFibrePresented.isPullback`;
187	* **the property clause** — that each represented pullback is an open immersion.  Supplied
188	  here by `W.ι` being an open immersion, which is free.
189	
190	What is *not* free, and is the whole mathematical content, is `exists_factor`: a class that
191	agrees with a chart value must come from the locus.  For the Abel chart that is the relative
192	form of DAT-C GAP-2 (uniqueness of the normalized effective representative) fed through the
193	classifier — so the CERT-Σ gate is real, but it gates ONE field of ONE structure rather than
194	the whole certificate. -/
195	theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented {X : Scheme.{u}}
196	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
197	    (D : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),
198	      ChartFibrePresented C f g) :
199	    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f := by
200	  refine MorphismProperty.relative.of_exists fun T g => ?_
201	  exact ⟨(D T g).W, yoneda.map (D T g).r, (D T g).W.ι, (D T g).isPullback,
202	    inferInstance⟩
203	
204	/-! ## The criterion is not vacuous
205	
206	A structure whose hard field is an existential can be inhabited for trivial reasons, and a
207	criterion built on one is then worthless.  This section rules that out **by proof** rather
208	than by inspection: the datum is unconstructible exactly when it must be. -/
209	
210	/-- **Non-vacuity of `ChartFibrePresented`, from the necessary direction.**
211	
212	If a chart map fails to be injective on the points of even one test, then no family of
213	`ChartFibrePresented` data exists for it.  In particular the criterion cannot be satisfied
214	for the *unrestricted* Abel chart, whose non-injectivity is the linear system `|D|`
215	(`Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:54`): the criterion's hypothesis is genuinely as strong as the
216	conclusion, and `exists_factor` is not a clause one can talk one's way past.
217	
218	The proof composes the two halves of this file, which is the point of having both. -/
219	theorem isEmpty_forall_chartFibrePresented_of_not_injective {X : Scheme.{u}}
220	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ)
221	    (hT : ¬ Function.Injective (f.app T)) :
222	    IsEmpty (∀ (T' : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T' ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),
223	        ChartFibrePresented C f g) :=
224	  ⟨fun D => hT (injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf
225	    (isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented f D) T)⟩
226	
227	/-- The same statement in the form a lane will meet it: the criterion's input **implies**
228	elementwise injectivity on every test.  So a lane that cannot prove uniqueness of the
229	normalized effective representative cannot supply the datum either — the CERT-Σ gate is not
230	an artefact of how `IsChartUniv` was pinned. -/
231	theorem injective_of_chartFibrePresented {X : Scheme.{u}}
232	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
233	    (D : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),
234	      ChartFibrePresented C f g) (T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ) :
235	    Function.Injective (f.app T) :=
236	  injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf
237	    (isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented f D) T
238	
239	end
240	
241	end AlgebraicGeometry

22	`ChartFibrePresented C (abelSigmaChart …) g` at every test — the datum for the *unrestricted*

24	there says the `W` field "is already discharged — it is `chartLocus`".  So the open `V` never
25	enters the hypothesis, and one term gives back the unrestricted certificate:
26	
27	```
28	isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented _ fun T g => (h T g).some
29	  : IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (abelSigmaChart …)

33	`isOpenImmersion_presheaf_abelSigmaChart_of_isChartLocusFibre` and
34	`mono_abelSigmaChart_of_isChartLocusFibre` in `Picard/Pic0ChartLocusFibreGuard.lean`, together
35	with `not_isChartLocusFibre_of_not_injective` — the criterion's own emptiness guard, finally
36	instantiated at the Abel chart.  In `isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre` the restriction to `V` is

77	  well-gated one; it discharges no antecedent.  `rep` (divisor representability) is a hypothesis

description: "Arguing \"h^0 >= 2 so the map is non-injective\" fails at the exact degree a construction pins, where the rank anchor forces h^0 = 1"

When judging whether a map out of a divisor scheme is injective, do NOT reason from the generic behaviour of linear systems. At the degree the construction actually pins, the numbers may be forced the other way.

Measured 2026-07-29 (run 0088, AJCR; refuted by ajcr-p3, I-0903): I argued the Abel chart is generically non-injective because the fibre is `|D| = P(H^0(O(D)))`, positive-dimensional when `h^0 > 1`. But the atlas reads at `deg D = g` (`chartTwist`'s target), and there with `Subsingleton H^1(O(D))` the rank anchor `h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one` (`AlgebraicJacobian/RiemannRoch/FLVClass.lean:412`) forces `h^0 = deg + chi = g + (1 - g) = 1` **exactly**. The fibre is a single point precisely where it is used, so the `|D|` argument is unavailable at the only degree that matters.

**Why it matters beyond the slip:** three file headers in AJCR blame `|D|` for the unrestricted certificate's failure. They may be right that it fails and wrong about why — which relocates the whole question (to whether a divisor-scheme point can have non-vanishing `H^1`, i.e. to the carve). A wrong *reason* attached to a right *conclusion* survives every census and misdirects whoever prices the leaf next.

**How to apply:** before using a dimension/genericity argument, substitute the construction's pinned numerical values (degree, twist exponent, genus) and check whether an anchor identity collapses them. In this project the anchor is `h^0 = deg + chi` under fibrewise `H^1`-vanishing. Also: I asserted this to two lanes before checking, so the retraction cost three messages — verify the numerics before broadcasting a route judgement.

Related: [[converse-checked-reduction-can-still-be-false]] (same file, same session), [[goals-measure-difficulty-not-ingredients]], [[gap-count-vs-gap-cost]].
---
name: two-refutations-are-not-inhabitation
description: Refuting a coupled hypothesis at both ends of its parameter feels like a non-vacuity proof; it is two refutations and leaves the pair unmeasured
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 6591cb6d-f3af-4d86-8ccc-8f880b70cebb
  modified: 2026-07-29T15:07:32.537Z
---

For a coupled hypothesis `(h1 V, h2 V)` sharing a parameter `V`, measuring both endpoints
invites a satisfying-sounding conclusion: "at `V = ⊥`, `h1` is free and `h2` impossible; at
`V = ⊤`, `h2` is free and `h1` maximal — so the coupling carries real content and is not
vacuous." **The last clause does not follow.** Non-vacuity of the pair needs a `V` where *both*
hold, or a refutation at *every* `V`. Two bad endpoints give neither: they are two refutations,
and they are equally consistent with the pair being unsatisfiable everywhere.

Measured 2026-07-29 (ajcr-p1, AJCR, caught by a fresh-context `work-reviewer` pass, I-1012).
I landed both endpoints sorry-free and axiom-clean, then wrote "these two together are the
non-vacuity check for the coupled assembly" into the module header. The mathematics survived all
seven audit items; only that noun was wrong.

**Why:** the endpoint work is genuinely informative — it proves any working `V` must be a proper
intermediate value, which promotes a "bookkeeping" side condition (here: openness of the chart
locus) to load-bearing. That real gain is what makes the overreach feel earned. The tell is
grammatical: "the pair has content" and "the pair has an inhabitant" are different claims, and
endpoint refutations only license the first.

**How to apply:** state endpoint results as a *conditional* ("any `V` that works must be
strictly between") and never as existence. Keep "inhabitation of the pair is unmeasured at every
parameter" as an explicit open line in the same docstring, so the next reader cannot mistake the
localisation for a satisfiability witness. Then look for the second-order leak: a *different*
form of the consumer (e.g. an instance-binder version rather than the explicit-hypothesis one)
may still go through at the cheap endpoint, and a refutation aimed at one spelling does not
constrain the other.

8	/-!
9	# DECIDING THE FORK: what non-injectivity of the unrestricted Abel chart actually costs
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusFibreGuard.lean` makes the fork precise and machine-checked:
12	`IsChartLocusFibre` implies the Abel chart is a monomorphism, which three headers
13	(`Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:54`, `Pic0ChartPair.lean:14`,
14	`Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean:214`) assert it is not.  Exactly one side is right, and
15	the guard leaves the deciding statement — non-injectivity — as prose.
16	
17	**This file reduces that statement to divisor data.**  The reduction is what was missing: the
18	Abel chart's app does not take divisors, it takes `D.left`-points, so "two divisors in one
19	linear system" is not by itself a witness.  Reading `abelChartApp_eq`
20	(`Pic0ChartCoverageAbel.lean:105`), a point `x : Y ⟶ D.left` is sent to the **pair**
21	
22	  `⟨x ≫ D.hom, chartValue … (rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk x rfl))⟩`
23	
24	so a non-injectivity witness owes *two* agreements, not one: the Σ-components `x ≫ D.hom` must
25	agree before the classes are in the same type at all.  That is the trap the c9b row names.
26	
27	## What is proved here
28	
29	The reduction, in the direction a witness-builder needs, and its converse:
30	
31	* `not_injective_abelSigmaChart_of_points` — from two `D.left`-points over one test with
32	  **equal structure morphism** and **equal chart value** but distinct as points, the Abel chart
33	  fails to be injective; `not_isChartLocusFibre_of_points` composes that with the guard to
34	  refute `IsChartLocusFibre`.
35	* `not_isChartLocusFibre_of_divFamZar` — the same reduction **reparameterised onto divisor
36	  families**: two distinct elements of `divFamZar C π n T` with equal chart value.  Here the
37	  Σ-component hypothesis is not passed in: both points are `(rep.homEquiv.symm sᵢ).left`, whose
38	  structure morphism is the test's own by `Over.w`, so `hstruct` holds by construction.
39	  **This is a change of parameterisation, not a strengthening** — the two forms are
40	  inter-derivable (from the family form, take `T := Over.mk (x₁ ≫ D.hom)` and use
41	  `rep.homEquiv.injective` for distinctness), so `hstruct` is absorbed by the choice of test
42	  rather than eliminated.  Its value is that the family form is the shape a divisor argument
43	  produces, with no scheme-theoretic side condition to discharge first.
44	* `abelChartApp_inj_iff` — the unfolded shape of injectivity at a test, by `Iff.rfl`.  A
45	  documentation lemma only: it has no call site below, and `abelChartApp_eq`
46	  (`Pic0ChartCoverageAbel.lean:105`) already exposes both components.
47	
48	## What is NOT proved here, stated so this file is not over-read
49	
50	**Nothing here exhibits a curve on which the hypothesis holds, and no theorem below closes the
51	fork.**  Every statement here is an implication whose antecedent is open.  What remains is
52	exactly:
53	
54	  for some curve, some test `T`, and some `n`: two *distinct* elements of `divFamZar C π n T`
55	  whose `chartValue` agree.
56	
57	Three things to know before pricing that, and the third is the one that moves.
58	
59	1. Over a field test it is the classical `h⁰(𝒪(D)) ≥ 2 ⇒ |D|` has two points.
60	   `Scheme.CurveDivisor.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_h0_one` (`RiemannRoch/EffectiveUniqueness.lean:144`)
61	   is the exact boundary: uniqueness holds **at** `h⁰ = 1`, so the hypothesis to arrange is
62	   `h⁰ ≥ 2`.  It is the statement to contradict, not to apply.
63	2. The passage from two *divisors* to two distinct *elements of `divFamZar`* is not free: the
64	   families are a quotient of local-equation data (`DivisorFamilyZar.lean:235`), so distinct
65	   divisors need not give distinct families until that equivalence is read.  Nothing here
66	   assumes otherwise.
67	3. **`n` is not free.**  At `n = g` the chart's own degree calibration makes the *fibrewise*
68	   linear system a single point for free: over a field `K`, an effective `K`-divisor of degree
69	   `g` with `Subsingleton H¹` has `h⁰ = 1` exactly (`degAt_chartTwist`'s `+g` discussion in
70	   `Pic0ChartLocus.lean:178-201`, and the rank anchor
71	   `h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one`, `RiemannRoch/FLVClass.lean:412`, giving
72	   `h⁰ = g + (1 − g) = 1`).  So the *fibrewise* form of the headers' reason — a
73	   positive-dimensional `|D|` — is unavailable at `n = g` wherever `H¹` vanishes.
74	
75	**AND HERE IS THE LIMIT OF THAT OBSERVATION, which item 3 must not be read past.**  Every anchor
76	in item 3 is fibrewise over one field: `CurveDivisor` over `K`, `h⁰` a `finrank` over `K`,
77	`degAt` evaluated at `overSpec k K`-points.  The obligation is **general-test**: injectivity of
78	`.app (op Y)` at arbitrary `Y`, and correspondingly distinctness in `divFamZar C π n T` at
79	arbitrary `T`.  A fibrewise anchor does not settle a general-test statement, and the brick that
80	would bridge them is *relative* GAP-2 — exactly `ChartFibrePresented.exists_factor`
81	(`Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean:140`), which `Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean:160-161` names as
82	"the relative form of DAT-C GAP-2" and which **nothing in the tree produces**: no declaration
83	concludes `s₁ = s₂` for two `divFamZar` sections from an equality of their classes.
84	
85	So item 3 **relocates** the fork; it does not shrink it.  What it changes is what a witness
86	should aim at: a bare "two divisors in one linear system" is the wrong target, because at `n = g`
87	with `h¹ = 0` there are none fibrewise — so a witness wants a point of the divisor scheme where
88	`H¹` fails to vanish, or a genuinely relative failure of uniqueness that no fibre sees.  Which
89	of those two it is, is undecided here.  (The degree-`g`/`h⁰ = 1` link is `ajcr-p4`'s measurement,
90	I-0888; the fibrewise/general-test caveat is a fresh-context review's, I-0923/I-0924.)
91	-/

122	theorem abelChartApp_inj_iff (Y : Scheme.{u}) :
123	    Function.Injective ((abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg).app (op Y))
124	      ↔ Function.Injective (fun x : Y ⟶ D.left =>
125	          (⟨x ≫ D.hom, ⟨chartValue C π n m Z (Over.mk (x ≫ D.hom))
126	              (rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk x rfl)),
127	            chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup C π n m Z hdeg _ _⟩⟩ :
128	            (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op Y))) :=
129	  Iff.rfl

133	/-- **Two `D.left`-points over one test with the same chart value refute the certificate.**
134	
135	The hypotheses are exactly the two agreements `abelChartApp_eq` demands — equal structure
136	morphism (`hstruct`) and equal chart value after that identification (`hval`) — together with
137	distinctness of the points themselves.
138	
139	Note `hval` is stated at the *transported* family: once `hstruct` identifies the Σ-components,
140	both chart values live over `Over.mk (x₁ ≫ D.hom)` and the equation typechecks. -/
141	theorem not_injective_abelSigmaChart_of_points {Y : Scheme.{u}} (x₁ x₂ : Y ⟶ D.left)
142	    (hne : x₁ ≠ x₂) (hstruct : x₁ ≫ D.hom = x₂ ≫ D.hom)
143	    (hval : chartValue C π n m Z (Over.mk (x₁ ≫ D.hom))
144	        (rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk x₁ rfl))
145	      = chartValue C π n m Z (Over.mk (x₁ ≫ D.hom))
146	          (rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk x₂ hstruct.symm))) :
147	    ¬ Function.Injective ((abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg).app (op Y)) := by
148	  intro hinj
149	  refine hne (hinj ?_)
150	  -- both values are Σ-elements over the *same* structure morphism after `hstruct`
151	  refine Over.sigmaExtension_ext (pic0TypeFunctor C) hstruct ?_
152	  -- the transport of `x₂`'s family along `mkCongr hstruct` is `x₂` read over `x₁`'s base
153	  have hmap : (divFunctor C π n).map (Over.mkCongr hstruct).op
154	        (rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk x₂ rfl))
155	      = rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk x₂ hstruct.symm) := by
156	    rw [← rep.homEquiv_comp]
157	    exact congrArg rep.homEquiv (Over.OverMorphism.ext (Category.id_comp x₂))
158	  have hnat := ConcreteCategory.congr_hom
159	    ((chartValueTrans C π n m Z hdeg).naturality (Over.mkCongr hstruct).op)
160	    (rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk x₂ rfl))
161	  refine hnat.symm.trans ?_
162	  rw [ConcreteCategory.comp_apply, hmap]
163	  exact Subtype.ext hval.symm

172	    (hval : chartValue C π n m Z (Over.mk (x₁ ≫ D.hom))
173	        (rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk x₁ rfl))
174	      = chartValue C π n m Z (Over.mk (x₁ ≫ D.hom))
175	          (rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk x₂ hstruct.symm))) :
176	    ¬ IsChartLocusFibre C π n rep m Z hdeg :=

192	    (s₁ s₂ : divFamZar C π n T) (hne : s₁ ≠ s₂)

199	  have hs₂ : x₂ ≫ D.hom = T.hom := Over.w _

201	  -- `Over.homMk xᵢ` recovers the slice morphism `rep.homEquiv.symm sᵢ` was, hence `sᵢ`
202	  have hrec₁ : rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk x₁ hs₁) = s₁ := by

PicEtAff.unit (:377), the target of relPicToPicEt (PicEtUnit.lean:126), is mk at the TRIVIAL cover `.self A` alone. So honesty says no nontrivial etale cover is needed on that piece -- exactly what the one-step plus construction exists to permit to fail.

THE PROJECT SAYS SO WHERE IT MEASURED IT: Pic0ChartHonest.lean's own "does not give" -- honesty holds "OVER Spec E.Carrier, NOT over Spec A", bought by CHANGING THE BASE, and "Nothing here performs that descent".

21	(`Picard/JacobianData.lean`) has **four** fields — `J`, `rep`, `locallyOfFiniteType`,
22	`quasiCompact` — and its every producer from an atlas takes a fourth input on top of `hf` and the

30	import closure, and a name outside the closure is not a name).  So a session that discharged all
31	three tracked antecedents would still not have produced a `JacobianData C`, and nothing in the
32	tree produces `hlft` **at a chart of an atlas** — `locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom`
33	(`JacobianDataCharts.lean`) is the only route to the glued object's certificate and it *takes*
34	`hlft` as a hypothesis.  The DAT-glue route does not escape this either: `PicRepDatum.lft` is a

36	an assumption there too.

39	and which are corrected here rather than annotated:
40	
41	* it does not claim `Challenge.lean` routes through `JacobianData`.  The frozen `Jacobian` is a
42	  `sorry` and does not import this layer; `Jacobian C := (jacobianData C).J` is the *planned*
43	  discharge route recorded in `JacobianData.lean`/`JacobianDataCharts.lean`, and no `jacobianData`
44	  producer exists in either project;
45	* it does not claim the certificate is untracked on the board.  The `dat-glue` row has named "the
46	  locally-of-finite-type certificate" in its title since 2026-07-16.  What was missing is a proof,
47	  not a mention.
48	
49	## What is actually owed, and it is much less than the gap suggests
50	
51	`Picard/Pic0ChartPair.lean` states, in prose, that the certificate is "inherited by every
52	restriction: being locally of finite type is local on the source, and an open immersion is
53	locally of finite type".  That sentence is correct and had never been proved — the shape this

143	/-- **The structure morphism of the `i`-th chart of the mixed-parameter atlas** is the
144	inclusion of `V i` followed by the structure morphism of the `i`-th representing object.

149	exponent `m i` and the chart index `Z i` do not occur on the right-hand side: the finiteness of a
150	chart is independent of the heterogeneity this atlas exists to permit. -/
151	lemma chartHom_mixedParamChart {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
152	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
153	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
154	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
155	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
156	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
157	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens) (i : ι) :
158	    chartHom C (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V) i = (V i).ι ≫ (D i).hom :=
159	  (chartHom_restrictChart _ (V i) i).trans (by rw [chartHom_abelSigmaChart])

164	/-- **THE FOURTH ANTECEDENT OF THE NORTH STAR, DISCHARGED AT THE REAL ATLAS**: each chart of the
165	mixed-parameter atlas is locally of finite type over the base field as soon as its representing
166	object is.
167	
168	This is the `hlft` hypothesis that `JacobianData.ofCharts` and all three of its variants carry
169	and that the board's three-antecedent picture omits.  `Pic0ChartPair.lean` asserts the inheritance
170	in prose; this is the proof, and it consumes nothing but `chartHom_mixedParamChart` and mathlib's
171	composition instance — an open immersion is locally of finite type and the property is stable
172	under composition.

174	The hypothesis is a statement about the divisor scheme alone.  In particular it does not mention
175	`pic⁰`, the chart parameter, the twist, or the open `V i` — so it is discharged for *every*
176	restriction of a chart at once, and a lane that produces `rep` at a parameter automatically
177	supplies it whenever the representing object is of finite type over `k`. -/
178	theorem locallyOfFiniteType_chartHom_mixedParamChart {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
179	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
180	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
181	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
182	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
183	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
184	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens)
185	    (hD : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (D i).hom) (i : ι) :

195	`JacobianData.locallyOfFiniteType` field itself, from a property of the divisor schemes.

197	`locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom` descends the certificate from the charts (the property is local on
198	the source and the glue maps cover), and the previous theorem supplies the charts.  Note that no
199	finiteness of the index type is used anywhere on this route: the certificate descends to an
200	infinite atlas exactly as it does to a finite one, which matters because the classical atlas is
201	indexed by divisor classes. -/
202	theorem locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom_mixedParamChart {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
203	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
204	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
205	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
206	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
207	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
208	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens)
209	    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V i))
210	    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
211	      (Sigma.desc (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V))]
212	    (hD : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (D i).hom) :
213	    LocallyOfFiniteType (gluedHom C (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V) hf) :=
214	  locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom C _ hf
215	    (locallyOfFiniteType_chartHom_mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V hD)
